Series::tracks_slope_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::tracks_slope_() const -> Series&
Series::tracks_slope_(bool enabled) const -> Series&

What It Does¶

tracks_slope_() mutates whether this Series is tracked for reverse-mode sensitivity.

This is the root opt-in switch for most autograd examples in the Series reference. If you want a leaf to receive stored sensitivity after a later reverse() call, this is the method you turn on before building the forward computation.

The underscore matters. This is a mutating state-control method, not a value-returning numeric transform.

Mathematically, this method does not compute a derivative and does not run the chain rule. It only decides whether this Series should behave as a leaf that can later receive stored sensitivity from reverse().

That is why tracks_slope_() belongs at the beginning of the workflow, while reverse() belongs at the end:

  1. mark the leaf with tracks_slope_()

  2. build the forward computation

  3. call reverse() on the final result

  4. inspect the stored value with sensitivity()

Parameters¶

enabled (bool)

Whether tracking should be enabled after the call.

  • true: mark the series as tracked

  • false: mark the series as untracked

The zero-argument overload is shorthand for tracks_slope_(true).

Returns¶

Series& The current Series, so the mutating call can chain naturally when useful.

State Effects¶

Changing this flag affects later reverse-mode behavior directly:

  • when enabled, future differentiable computations can accumulate sensitivity back onto this series

  • when disabled, future reverse passes do not store sensitivity here as a tracked leaf

The current implementation also clears any stored sensitivity when this state is changed. That keeps old sensitivity state from being mistaken for the new tracking regime.

Examples¶

Example 1. The no-argument form is shorthand for turning tracking on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
std::cout << "before=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.tracks_slope_();
std::cout << "after_enable_default=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.tracks_slope_(false);
std::cout << "after_disable=" << (x.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

The no-argument overload means “enable tracking.” It does not mean “toggle to the opposite state.”

Output¶

before=false
after_enable_default=true
after_disable=false

Example 2. The tracking flag decides whether a reverse pass is even possible. The same objective, reversed once without a tracked leaf and once with one:

auto untracked = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
auto tracked = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
tracked.tracks_slope_(true);

try {
  untracked.mul(2.0).sum().reverse();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << "untracked: " << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

tracked.mul(2.0).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "tracked_has_dL_dx=" << (tracked.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "tracked_dL_dx=" << tracked.sensitivity() << "\n";

Both forward computations are the same scalar objective L = 2x₁ + 2x₂ + 2x₃. The mathematical sensitivity exists in either case, but only the tracked leaf produces a connected graph; reversing the untracked one raises instead of storing nothing.

Output¶

untracked: series_tape::backpropagate: objective does not track slope and has no source link; nothing to differentiate (a constant, or built only from non-differentiable ops)
tracked_has_dL_dx=true
tracked_dL_dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2]

Example 3. Disabling tracking clears the currently stored sensitivity for that leaf.

auto x = pluss::make_series({3.0, 4.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.mul(2.0).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "before_disable=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
x.tracks_slope_(false);
std::cout << "after_disable=" << (x.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

before_disable=true
after_disable=false

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • This method changes tracking state; it is not itself a differentiable operation.

  • The zero-argument overload means “enable,” not “toggle.”

  • Disabling tracking does more than prevent future storage. It also clears the current stored sensitivity state.

Summary¶

Use tracks_slope_() before the forward pass to mark leaves that should later receive reverse-mode sensitivity, and use tracks_slope_(false) when you want that leaf to stop participating as a tracked source.

See Also¶

  • Series::tracks_slope: inspect the current tracking flag.

  • Series::reverse: populate sensitivity on tracked leaves.

  • Series::clear_sensitivity: clear stored sensitivity without disabling tracking.
